info.title: OpenDDE Harness TUI RPC
info.description: JSON-RPC 2.0 contract for the registered Python TUI handlers and their notifications. Handlers are authoritative; tests/test_tui_rpc_schema.py validates real wire results and emissions. TypeScript is generated by scripts/gen-rpc-types.mjs (--check in CI).

methods.name: session.list
methods.summary: List tui-channel sessions sorted by updated_at descending.

schema.description: Positive limits slice TUI sessions after sorting by updated_at descending; zero, negative and non-integer limits are ignored.

methods.name: session.create
methods.summary: Mint a fresh lazy session; ignores all parameters.

methods.name: session.resume
methods.summary: Resume a session_id; missing or unknown ids mint a fresh session with empty messages.

methods.name: session.delete
methods.summary: Delete a session file and invalidate its cache entry.

schema.description: Full session_key as sent by the UI.

methods.name: session.info
methods.summary: The init bundle for a session already open, without opening or replacing anything.

schema.description: Full session_key; absent answers for the defaults a new session would start on.

methods.name: session.most_recent
methods.summary: Return the most-recently-updated tui session key.

methods.name: session.title
methods.summary: Get or set the title of a session.

schema.description: When present, set as the new title; when absent, return the current title.

methods.name: session.clear
methods.summary: Wipe a session's messages in place, keeping the same session_id.

session_id.description: The same session_key (no new id minted).

cleared.description: True when the in-place wipe ran.

methods.name: session.undo
methods.summary: Drop the last n turns of a session (default 1).

context_used.description: What the conversation holds now the exchange is gone, in tokens, so a status line can stop reporting a window that has not been that full since. Null where a compaction marker the backend replays stands in front of the history, which is the answer session.info gives for that same session. Absent when nothing was removed.

methods.name: session.export
methods.summary: Render a session transcript to a Markdown file and return its path.

schema.description: Session id, prefix or full key; omitted or unknown ids return exported=false, path=null, reason=not_found.

exported.description: True when a Markdown file was written.

path.description: Absolute path of the written file, or null on failure.

reason.description: Failure reason when not exported: not_found | ambiguous | write_failed.

candidates.description: Candidate full keys when reason is ambiguous.

methods.name: session.instructions
methods.summary: List the AGENTS.md / ODH.md files the next turn will send, or switch one off for this session.
methods.description: Backs /memory. Switching a file off lasts as long as the gateway process and is never written to config. A toggle naming nothing the search found changes nothing and returns the reason in error.

schema.description: Omitted or list reports; on / off switch one file for this session only.
Which file to switch: its absolute path, its shown name, or its basename when unambiguous.
Whose view this is. on / off apply to this conversation alone; omitted describes the defaults a new session would start on.

cwd.description: The directory the search ran from.

changed.description: The shown name of the file just switched, else null.

error.description: Why nothing was switched, in one line, else null.

methods.name: turn.send
methods.summary: Send a user message to a session and start a turn.

methods.name: turn.subscribe
methods.summary: Subscribe to streaming TurnEvent notifications for a session.

methods.name: turn.unsubscribe
methods.summary: Stop receiving notifications; turn itself continues.

methods.name: turn.cancel
methods.summary: Cancel the active scheduler handle; no active turn returns cancelled=false.

methods.name: model.options
methods.summary: List providers and the current selection; optionally skip catalogues, expand only one provider, or ask the declared endpoints what they serve first.

params.name: refresh
params.description: Fetch every declared endpoint's /models before answering, the way pi refreshes its model catalogs when its picker opens. Failures come back in refresh_errors; the rows are the last known list either way.

default_model.description: agents.defaults.model: what new sessions start on.

refresh_errors.description: By provider id, the endpoints a refresh could not ask, each with the sentence it failed with; `*` when the service itself could not be asked.

methods.name: model.save_key
methods.summary: Write a provider's credential: a key, or the address and wire of a provider this config declares.

params.name: api_key
params.description: Empty for a provider reached without one: a self-hosted endpoint that wants no key, or a built-in whose key is already in the environment. Required wherever a key is what reaches the vendor.

params.name: base_url
params.description: Where a provider this config declares lives. Required together with api, and meaningless for one of pi's own, which carries its own address.

params.name: api
params.description: The wire that address serves, one of the seven the model service implements (it names them all when it refuses one). Required together with base_url.

methods.name: model.declare_provider
methods.summary: Declare an OpenAI-compatible endpoint this config does not hold: its id, its address and a key if it wants one. What it serves is read from its /models, the way pi treats OpenRouter.

params.name: provider
params.description: The id the entry is filed under, and the prefix of every model id it serves. Never one of pi's own: pi ships those with their own address and catalogue, and the provider list offers them a credential instead.

params.name: base_url
params.description: Where the endpoint lives: an http:// or https:// address, dialled as it is written and never guessed at.

params.name: model
params.description: Model ids typed by hand, comma-separated, for an endpoint that publishes no list at GET /models. Otherwise empty: the list is discovered.

params.name: api_key
params.description: Empty for the common case: a self-hosted server usually wants no key. Written, never read back -- the row returned carries no credential.

discovered.description: How many models the endpoint published when asked just now.

methods.name: model.logout
methods.summary: pi's /logout: forget a provider's stored credential -- the grant of a sign-in, or its key -- and keep what the entry declares.

forgotten.description: False when there was nothing stored to forget.

methods.name: model.scope
methods.summary: pi's scoped models: read the saved scope (agents.scopedModels), or write it when `write` is set. null is every model.

methods.name: model.overlay
methods.summary: Set one field of the current model's declared row in providers.<id>.models (persisted; default clears it and the catalogue or the global setting applies).

params.name: value
params.description: Read for the field named: a thinking level, a token count (128k allowed), on/off, a number, or free text. `default` clears whichever field it is.

context_window.description: The window the loop runs with after the change, for a field that sizes a request.

methods.name: model.login
methods.summary: Run a provider's OAuth sign-in and answer when it has stored a credential. Every step pi reports on the way arrives as a login.step notification carrying this login's id.

params.name: login_id
params.description: The id this flow's login.step notifications will carry, chosen by the client so it can tell its own flow's steps from another's before the first one arrives. Minted by the gateway when absent.

login_id.description: The id its login.step notifications carried, so a client can tell which flow finished.

methods.name: model.login_answer
methods.summary: Answer the step a running sign-in is waiting on: the option id of a select, the pasted code of a manual_code.

answered.description: False when nothing was waiting: the login ended, or the browser callback answered first.

methods.name: model.login_cancel
methods.summary: Cancel a running sign-in. Idempotent: a login that already ended answers false.

methods.name: config.get
methods.summary: Read exactly two flat keys: tui.theme, tui.show_token_usage. These are config keys, not RPC method names.

schema.description: If omitted, return all whitelisted fields. Unknown keys are silently dropped.

methods.name: config.set
methods.summary: Write one of the four config.get keys, or key=model to switch a session/default model. A model value is `<provider>/<model>`; a bare id names no provider and is refused.

params.name: session_id
params.summary: Scopes a model switch to one conversation.

params.name: scope
params.summary: How far a model switch reaches: this conversation, or what new ones start on.

methods.name: system.hello
methods.summary: Initial handshake (must be the first RPC call from client).

methods.name: system.ping
methods.summary: Liveness probe.

methods.name: system.version
methods.summary: Report server / schema / package versions.

schema_version.description: OpenRPC info.version mirrored back to client.

methods.name: cli.dispatch
methods.summary: Dispatch an OpenDDE Harness CLI command in-process, capture rich-rendered output.
methods.description: D7 mixed-mode main channel: read-only CLI commands route through cli.dispatch and reuse the Typer CLI's Rich rendering. width is contract-required (client measures Ink container, server cannot guess). See design.md §3 D7.

schema.description: Pre-tokenized argv (TUI side has already shlex-split).
Ink container width in cells; required for Rich Console wrapping.
Override the default 30s timeout for long-running commands.

methods.name: setup.status
methods.summary: Report whether an LLM provider and the Protein Design compute are configured.
methods.description: Called by the TUI at startup. Reads ~/.opendde_harness/config.json; provider_configured is false when the config cannot be read, in which case error names the remedy. compute_configured is present only when the config was read.

methods.name: reload.mcp
methods.summary: No-op: always returns ok=true, reloaded=0, tools_changed=false.
methods.description: MUST NOT throw. hermes UI useConfigSync.ts:202 polls every 5s; throwing would spam logs. v0.1 implementation returns {ok: true} unconditionally. See design.md §3a.2.

methods.name: commands.catalog
methods.summary: Dynamic CLI command catalog reflected from the Typer app (replaces v0.0.2 -32012 stub).
methods.description: Reflects opendde_harness.cli.commands.app to build a slash-command catalog consumed by the TUI's alias / prefix-1-match / multi-match-ambiguous logic in src/commands/registry.ts. Filters out _DISPATCH_BLACKLIST entries (gateway / provider login / channels login / sandbox shell / tui / onboard) and agent-without-message. See harness-command-catalog-dynamic design.md §D1-D2.

methods.name: session.close
methods.summary: Flush a known session; absent or unknown ids are ignored.

methods.name: session.branch
methods.summary: Fork a nonempty session; unknown or empty sources return null session_id and title.

methods.name: session.status
methods.summary: Render install-wide status plus usage for the requested session.

methods.name: terminal.resize
methods.summary: Record positive integer dimensions; invalid dimensions are ignored.

methods.name: slash.exec
methods.summary: Dispatch a slash command; failures are returned as output and optional warning.

methods.name: complete.slash
methods.summary: Stub: ignores parameters and returns no completions.

methods.name: complete.path
methods.summary: Stub: ignores parameters and returns no completions.

methods.name: approval.respond
methods.summary: Available with an approval broker. session_id is canonical; conversation_id is its fallback. Invalid or stale requests return ok=false.

methods.name: confirm.respond
methods.summary: Available with a confirm broker. Resolve a pending confirmation; stale ids return ok=false.

methods.name: clarify.respond
methods.summary: Available with a question broker. conversation_id takes precedence over request_id; cancelled resolves to the default answer.

JsonValue.description: Recursive JSON value type. Implemented as an unconstrained object in JSON Schema; downstream Pydantic uses typing.Any.

release_date.description: When this version shipped, from the changelog the package carries. Null when the install has no changelog to read.

project_instructions.description: The AGENTS.md / ODH.md files this session sends, outermost first. Listed, never quoted.

mcp_servers.description: Configured MCP servers. They connect on the session's first turn, so a freshly created session reports them not yet connected.

subscription.description: The model runs on a plan rather than per token, so no per-call price describes it. Read from the provider entry the model id names: a sign-in (`login: "oauth"`) is a plan, a key is metered.

auto_compact.description: Something will compact this session before its context window runs out: the backend server-side, or the context engine here.

SessionListItem.description: One row in the TUI session picker (gatewayTypes.ts SessionListItem).

ProjectInstructionFile.description: One AGENTS.md / ODH.md instruction file the session found. The list travels; the contents never do.

path.description: Absolute path, which is what /memory on|off names.

display.description: How it is shown: relative to the work-tree root, ~/... for the user scope, absolute otherwise.

size.description: Size on disk in bytes, which is not the size sent when truncated is true.

truncated.description: Larger than the 32 KiB per-file cap, so only its head is sent.

skipped.description: Found but not sent: the 128 KiB total was already spent by nearer files.

enabled.description: False when /memory off switched it off for this session.

changed.description: Its content differs from what this session first saw in it. The agent can write files, so a change nobody at the keyboard made is worth showing.

parameters.description: JSON Schema for the tool's input arguments.

ModelOptionProvider.description: One provider row. `slug` is a pi provider id: the key of the `providers` entry it describes, and the prefix of every model id in `models`.

auth_type.description: How this provider is reached: a sign-in, an address this config declares, or a key.

key_env.description: The environment variable that already supplies this provider's key, or null when none does.

models.description: Qualified ids (`<provider>/<model>`), which is what config.set and model.add_model take.

models_loaded.description: False when only configured, curated and current models are included; request this slug to expand its catalogue.

auth_methods.description: Every way in pi offers for this provider, in pi's own order, read from pi's own provider objects. Two of them is what a client offers a choice between; empty when the model service could not be asked.

login_label.description: pi's own label for the sign-in option (its `oauth.loginLabel`, e.g. "Sign in with SuperGrok or X Premium"), or null where pi carries none and its generic sentence applies.

key_label.description: pi's own name for this provider's key (its `apiKey.name`, e.g. "Anthropic API key").

needs_api_key.description: A key must be typed before this provider can serve anything.

needs_base_url.description: This provider is one the config declares, so its address and the wire it speaks must both be given.

base_url.description: The declared address as configured, for a form that prefills it; null for one of pi's own.

api.description: The wire the declared address serves, as configured; null for one of pi's own, which carries its own.

model_labels.description: Keyed by the model id as it appears in `models`.

ModelLabel.description: How a model reads to a person: the name its declared row gives it, else the one the model service reports, else the id with its provider prefix dropped.

cache_hit_percent.description: Share of the last call's prompt served from the provider's cache, 0-100; null when the call sent no prompt or the provider stated no cache figure.

cost_usd.description: Estimated cost of the last call in USD; null on a plan-billed provider, where no per-token figure exists.

list_cost_usd.description: What the call is worth at the vendor's published price, whoever is billing. What a plan-billed session can show beside its (sub) marker; null when no price is published for the model.

context_source.description: Which tier sized context_max; "unknown" with a zero context_max means no table lists the model.

context_compacted.description: The conversation was compacted after this call, so context_used describes a prompt that no longer exists. What the window holds is unknown until the next call reports; a status line shows "?" rather than the stale figure.

session_input_tokens.description: The session's total prompt tokens, cached ones included, from the same tracker /status reads. Every field above describes this turn or its last call; the session_* fields describe the session, so a footer showing the session's spend and a /status line reporting it cannot disagree.

session_cost_usd.description: What the vendor says the session has cost; null on a plan-billed provider, which states no per-token figure.

session_list_cost_usd.description: The session's spend at the vendor's published price, whoever is billing. This is the figure the footer shows. Null when no model used has a published price -- never zero for unknown.

session_calls.description: How many billed model calls the session has made.

stdout.description: Rich-rendered output with ANSI SGR sequences.

stderr.description: Error / warning output with ANSI SGR sequences.

error_code.description: Only present for timeout / not-dispatch-compatible cases (mirrors a JSON-RPC error code).

commands.description: Every CLI command the gateway will run for a slash, with what it is and what it takes. The set is exactly what cli.dispatch accepts, so a bare group head (`provider`) is absent: it is not a command and dispatch refuses it.

name.description: Space-separated argv without the leading slash, e.g. "provider list".

description.description: One line from the command's own Typer help or docstring.

argument_hint.description: Positional arguments, <required> and [optional], in declaration order, then any option the command cannot run without. Absent when the command takes none.

timeout_s.description: Seconds this command is allowed, where the ordinary slash timeout is not enough (a first `compute prepare` downloads model weights). Absent for everything else. The gateway applies the same figure itself; a client reads it to say that a command may take a while.

pairs.description: RETIRED WITH THE INK FRONT-END. Group heads only, which is why an entry here can be a group rather than a command; `commands` is what a client should read. Kept because the Ink client gates on non-empty pairs (createGatewayEventHandler.ts) and degrades to direct slash.exec without them. Remove this field when that client is deleted at the cut-over.

categories.description: Ordered category list: '(top-level)' first then alphabetical group names. Fully filtered groups (e.g. tui) do not appear.

skill_count.description: Total skill count from skill_forge store SQL count; 0 if DB missing (warning field then populated).

warning.description: Optional warning pushed to TUI activity strip (e.g. 'skill store not initialized').

ToolProgressEvent.description: Legacy event shape retained for clients; no current Python producer.

result_preview.description: The head of what the tool returned (up to 1 KiB), for the transcript row; what ctrl+o expands to. Not what the model was given.

truncated.description: Whether the result outran the preview, so expanding the row shows its head only.

CronDeliveredEvent.description: Legacy event shape retained for clients; no current Python producer.

CronMissedEvent.description: Legacy event shape retained for clients; no current Python producer.

TurnEvent.description: Discriminated union of turn streaming events. The 'type' field is the discriminator.

list_cost_usd.description: The session's spend at the vendor's published price, whoever is billing; what the footer opens on. Null when no model used has a published price.

context_used.description: What the stored conversation holds, in tokens, as the server estimates it. Null when nothing measures it: a compaction marker this session's backend replays stands in front of the history, so what the next call sends is the marker and not the messages it replaced. A status line shows "?" rather than a percentage of superseded history.

LoginStep.description: One step of pi's own sign-in flow, in pi's own shape and camelCase: four it reports (device_code, auth_url, info, progress) and two it waits for an answer to (select, manual_code). The 'type' field is the discriminator.
